text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Subsidiary of state oil firm NNPC indicted over fresh fuel scarcity; accused of failing to replenish stocks in Lagos area.
- Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group may resume oil production in the ethnic Ijaw areas as protesters end occupation of its oil flow stations.
- Shareholders association urges federal government to ban importation of cement to encourage local production.
- Many ailing banks appear ready for liquidation, having sold their assets ahead of 31 March government deadline to recapitalise or face being wound up.
- New decree gives state insurance firm NICON monopoly over insuring government firms.
- Foreign partner in Nigerian Ropes Plc, Bridon International of Britain, may increase its stake following visit of senior executive to Lagos.

- Secretary-general of Organisation of African Unity Salim Ahmed Salim calls for removal of visa restrictions among African nations to allow for free movement of goods and people; he was speaking at an OAU trade fair in Kaduna, northern Nigeria.
- Turnover on Nigerian stock exchange last week rose by 39.06 percent from the previous week while index improved by 2.9 percent.
